tldr: InfoQ argued on Oct 19 that agentic AI shifts distributed systems from functional decomposition to decision decomposition. A survey of trustworthy distributed ML followed on Oct 28.
whats_new: DistDebug-Bench (Nov 2) tests whether LLM agents can diagnose bugs in distributed systems, beyond the small self-contained modules existing benchmarks use.
why_it_matters: Agents are being placed inside distributed architectures, but there is little evidence yet that they can debug them; a benchmark is the first way to measure that.

beats.headline: Survey of security and trust in cloud-edge-IoT distributed ML
DistDebug-Bench targets agent debugging of distributed systems

open_questions: How do current LLM agents score on DistDebug-Bench?
Do agent frameworks adopt distributed-systems failure testing?
take_for_builders: Before giving an agent on-call duties in a multi-service system, run it on distributed-failure scenarios; single-module coding scores do not predict this.
